_comment: Canonical registry of knowledge modules and knowledge sets.
This is REPOSITORY SPECIFICATION METADATA. It is not the knowledge bundle
format, not an OKF schema, and not the runtime serialization of a profile's
knowledge selection. The bundle format is decided — U7 was resolved by
accepted ADR-0015, which adopts OKF v0.2 as the source representation;
choosing the profile serialization belongs to the profile schema, which does
not exist yet. JSON is used because it parses with the standard library in
both Node and Python, so scripts/check-knowledge.mjs runs before install and
reads structure rather than pattern-matching prose.
This file is the single source for module and set metadata. knowledge/INDEX.md
is the human-facing view of it, and check-knowledge.mjs asserts the two agree
in both directions so they cannot drift.
The toolchain, its conformance suite, and repository content admission are
implemented. The ADR-0015 12 obligation was discharged on 2026-08-16 after
independent review, so blockedByToolchain is false on every entry and
Validated and Packaged - post-toolchain lifecycle states - are representable
for a module that has earned them. The per-entry status fields below are the
authoritative answer for which modules those are. blockedByRollout is
unchanged and still holds household,
runbooks, and every set: authoring eligibility requires BOTH gates false.
Published additionally requires Proof B, for which no governed producer
exists (ADR-0016 5a).
Two freshness fields exist on a set and they are not the same thing:
freshnessPolicy  — when the COMPOSITION should be reviewed (prose)
maxFreshnessDays — the ceiling the set imposes on the MODULES it selects,
enforced at resolution; a required module staler than
this rejects the run.

modules.purpose: How this platform behaves, in the terms an agent must reason in.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Describes the operating model only; confers no authority and states no enforced threshold.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when an ADR changes the operating model.

modules.purpose: What lives in which repository root, and what does not belong there.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Names roots and their roles, never a file inventory. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when a taxonomy root is added, removed, or redefined.

modules.purpose: Instruction precedence, ADR immutability, and how a decision changes.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Describes the governance system, never the content of an individual decision. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the precedence order or the ADR lifecycle changes.

modules.purpose: How the workspace is assembled and how a change is landed.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Names no pinned version; the catalog and lockfile are authoritative for those. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the dependency-governance triad or the merge-gate model changes.

modules.purpose: The rules an agent writing code in this repository must hold.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. States that rules are enforced; never carries the enforced rule data itself. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the dependency-direction model or the language boundary changes.

modules.purpose: What a review looks for, and what a reviewable change contains.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Contains nothing about specific people or review history. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the pull-request template or the reporting obligations change.

modules.purpose: How API surface is authored so one definition produces every downstream artifact.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Names no endpoint path, hostname, or environment URL, and reproduces no generated document. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the contract-authoring model or the normalization pipeline changes.

modules.purpose: What every background worker owes the platform.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Names no broker address, queue endpoint, or connection detail, and carries no live worker state. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the worker runtime contract or the inference boundary changes.

modules.purpose: How agent runs execute, and where authority actually comes from.
modules.limitations: Portable projection only. Names no image digest, no profile contents, and no live run state. Grants nothing.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the runner concepts, the grant model, the effect-boundary semantics, the identity model, or the evidence contract change.

modules.purpose: How the platform behaves when parts of it are unreachable.
modules.limitations: No content authored. BOUNDED behaves as FAIL CLOSED until U1 is resolved, and the module must say so.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the degraded-mode classification changes, or when U1 resolves.

modules.purpose: The structure of the house: floors, areas, rooms, and how they relate.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Structure only; never occupancy, presence, or device state.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review on renovation, room repurposing, or a change to area naming.

modules.purpose: HVAC equipment mapping, zones, capacities, and documented operating limits.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Documented equipment limits are not the enforced safety envelope.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review on equipment replacement or service.

modules.purpose: What household security signals mean, and what the system does not detect.
modules.limitations: No content authored. The strictest module: no placement, no identifiers, no access history, no names.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review on a change to security equipment classes or signal semantics.

modules.purpose: Tariff and telemetry semantics: what the energy data means and how to read it.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Semantics only; no rate, price, or consumption value.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review on a tariff structure change or a change to upstream metric definitions.

modules.purpose: How to prove a repository change is sound, and what each check establishes.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Quotes no expected counts or sample output, both of which drift.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when a check is added or removed, or reporting obligations change.

modules.purpose: The ordered procedure for reasoning about a household incident.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Procedure only; carries no live state and no contact detail.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when escalation classes change or an incident class is added.

modules.purpose: When an agent must stop, and how it hands a situation to a human.
modules.limitations: No content authored. Describes when and how to hand over, never to whom.
modules.freshnessPolicy: Review when the stop conditions or the handover contract change.

sets.purpose: Reviewing a change before a pull request is opened.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: three required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. Composition only; it grants no capability.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review when the review conventions or the validation procedure change.
sets.rationale: A reviewer needs the governance model, the taxonomy, the review conventions, and the validation runbook. Degraded operation is included because a review must be able to judge failure-path changes. No household knowledge: a coding runner has no path to the house.

sets.purpose: Implementing a change in this repository on the local host.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: three required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. The optional API-contract module means two runs of this set can see different context; evidence records which.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review when the implementation rules, workspace conventions, or worker contract change.
sets.rationale: API contract conventions are optional rather than required because most changes do not touch API surface; a task that does may add it, which is why this set permits task additions.

sets.purpose: Reasoning about architecture and proposing decisions.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: two required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. Deliberately omits implementation and workspace modules, so a run using it cannot look up how to build what it proposes.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review when the runner model or the degraded-mode classification changes.
sets.rationale: Deliberately excludes the implementation and workspace modules. An architecture run reasons about the model, and loading implementation rules invites it to start editing.

sets.purpose: Answering questions about the state and structure of the house.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: four required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. Describes the house; carries no live state and confers no ability to read or change any device.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review on a change to household topology or security equipment classes.
sets.rationale: Household sets carry a shorter freshness window than coding sets because a stale house description is confidently wrong about physical reality. Developer-platform conventions are denied outright.

sets.purpose: Reasoning about comfort and HVAC behaviour.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: four required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. Documented equipment limits are not the enforced safety envelope, and this set grants no actuation.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review on equipment replacement or a change to comfort conventions.
sets.rationale: Topology is required, not optional: climate equipment is described per zone and a zone means nothing without the area mapping. Security semantics are denied — a comfort run has no business holding them.

sets.purpose: Reasoning about energy cost and load shifting.
sets.limitations: No version assigned: three required members are still unversioned, and no set has been released. Cost reasoning never justifies leaving the safety envelope, and this set grants no actuation.
sets.freshnessPolicy: Review on a tariff structure change or a change to upstream metric definitions.
sets.rationale: The narrowest household set. Climate and topology are optional because a cost question can be answered without them, and a pre-cooling proposal is where they become necessary.
